processing: Mostly fully oxidised black tea in orthodox and CTC, with some green tea also made on the estate.
harvest_season: No garden-specific calendar is documented; as with other Assam gardens, the May to June second flush is generally the most valued.
appearance_dry: Dark leaf with golden tips in high orthodox grades such as FTGFOP1.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, typical of a good Assam orthodox.
appearance_wet: Even coppery leaf in the clonal orthodox grades.
taste_profile: Known for a smoother cup than the Assam norm, with the malt of the region and less harsh grip.

brewing.notes: Try the orthodox grades plain first, since smoothness is the point. Three to four minutes is usually enough.

vintage_note: Sold by grade and season through importers, with high orthodox grades such as FTGFOP1 and clonal lots at the top. As usual for Assam, choose the latest available season and drink it within a year or two.
description:
Mangalam is a compact Assam estate of 118 hectares in Sivasagar district, reachable from the NH-37 highway. It is best known for a smoother style of tea and has found a following in Germany.

The estate makes orthodox and CTC, and a little green tea too. Its top orthodox grades may be labelled as clonal, meaning the leaf comes from selected propagated bushes and not seedlings.

Expect the malt typical of Assam, but with a gentler edge than the strong breakfast style. Three to four minutes works well, and it is worth trying the better lots without milk.

Check grade and season on the label. The name is common in India, so make sure the pack actually says Assam.
history: Little is documented about the garden's founding or early owners. Its modern reputation rests on orthodox tea sold abroad, especially to German buyers, and on higher prices earned by both its orthodox and CTC teas.
